newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab fund extends $20 credit line to two Gulf banks.
newsitem.headline: Arab fund extends $20 credit line to two Gulf banks.

text.p: The Arab Trade Financing Programme (AFTP) said on Wednesday it had signed agreements extending two credit lines of $10 million each to two Gulf banks.

"AFTP signed two credit agreements worth $20 million with Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait and the National Commercial Bank in their capacity as approved national agencies in Bahrain," an AFTP statement said.
It said the two agreements were aimed at providing means for re-financing 85 percent of credits offered by the two banks to clients involved in Arab trade.
AFTP is 50 percent owned by the Abu Dhabi-based Arab Monetary Fund -- the Arab world's premier financing institution -- and other institutions.
